column2: The new flag appears in the command's --help/usage text with a one-line description
Existing invocations without the new flag behave exactly as before
A flag that needs a value fails with a clear usage error when the value is missing
Every changed shell script passes bash -n
Shell changes work on macOS bash 3.2 and BSD tools (no GNU-only flags)
No `echo "$big" | grep -q` under pipefail; use here-strings
Every link and path you add or change resolves
Every command shown in the docs is copy-paste runnable against the current code
Actions are pinned to a major version or SHA, and the workflow still passes on every matrix entry
The change is verified on every OS/runtime in the CI matrix
Session and token lifetimes come from one configured value, not hard-coded constants
Token refresh happens before expiry and handles concurrent refreshes safely
Expiry checks tolerate client/server clock skew
Rejected requests get HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header
Rate-limit counters live in a store shared by every instance (not per-process memory)
The limit is enforced per API key and handles bursts at window boundaries
The migration has a tested down/rollback path or a documented restore plan
A backup or dry-run step runs before any destructive statement
Large deletes/updates run in batches with progress logging
Timestamps are stored in UTC and converted to the user's time zone only for display
Date logic is tested across DST transitions and at UTC+10/UTC-10 offsets
Before and after timings come from the same repeatable measurement
The optimisation targets the dominant cost shown by a profile
Tests share no mutable state and pass in random order
Tests do not depend on wall-clock time or sleeps; time is injected or faked
The layout works at 360px, 768px and 1280px widths
Text and controls meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 for body text)
Every interactive element is reachable and operable by keyboard
The upstream changelog's breaking changes are checked against this codebase
Lockfiles are regenerated by the package manager, not edited by hand
No secrets, tokens or credentials are logged, committed or printed
New credentials or permissions use the least privilege that works
Every reference is updated: code, tests, docs, config and scripts
A deprecated alias keeps the old name working if external callers exist
The new environment variable is documented with its default and effect
Behaviour when the variable is unset or empty is defined and tested
The JSON output has a stable, documented shape with no extra lines on stdout
Exit codes stay meaningful in JSON mode
CSV fields with commas, quotes and newlines are escaped (RFC 4180) and UTF-8 encoded
Exports stream rows instead of loading the whole dataset into memory
New logging is off by default or goes to stderr, never mixed into stdout output
